name: What paint sheen should I use for interior ceilings?

mainEntity.name: What paint sheen should I use for interior ceilings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Flat latex ceiling paint is standard for dry living spaces and bedrooms because it reflects almost no light, hiding drywall seams, tape joints, and surface imperfections. In high-humidity areas like bathrooms or unvented kitchens, a satin, eggshell, or dedicated kitchen-and-bath finish is preferred to resist moisture absorption and mildew. While sheen adds wipeability, higher-sheen finishes reveal subtle drywall flaws and roller marks. Choosing between them involves balancing ceiling smoothness against moisture exposure. If older drywall repairs or settling cracks exist, flat paint remains the most forgiving choice.
acceptedAnswer.description: Flat latex paint is ideal for living rooms and bedrooms to conceal surface imperfections, while satin or eggshell finishes perform best against moisture in bathrooms.
